name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPS-3M 'Mongrel'
description:
The KPS-3M Mongrel is Kang-Petrov's modular SMG platform designed to accept components scavenged from other weapons. The receiver has universal attachment points that mate with barrels, stocks, grips, and magazines from over forty different weapon systems. A Mongrel might have a Tessera barrel, a Crucible stock, and a Meridian magazine, all functioning together through Kang-Petrov's universal interface system.

The base Mongrel kit — receiver, bolt, and basic furniture — costs Φ300. Everything else is salvageable. Kang-Petrov publishes compatibility guides listing which components from which manufacturers fit the Mongrel's universal interface, and the community has expanded this list through experimentation. The weapon's reliability depends entirely on the quality of components used — a Mongrel built from premium salvage outperforms a Mongrel built from garbage.

The KPS-3M exists because weapons break, get abandoned, and accumulate in conflict zones faster than they can be manufactured or disposed of. The Mongrel transforms this surplus of parts into functional weapons, recycling the detritus of violence into tools for survival. It is simultaneously the most innovative and most desperate weapon in production.
specifications:
caliber: Variable (depends on barrel/magazine configuration)
effective_range: Variable (30-150m depending on build)
rate_of_fire: Variable (depends on bolt and caliber)
magazine_capacity: Variable (depends on magazine used)
weight: 1.5-3.0 kg (depends on configuration)
tactical_use: The Mongrel's tactical value is adaptability. In environments where resupply is impossible, the ability to scavenge components from any weapon system and build a functional SMG is invaluable. Operators in prolonged sieges, behind enemy lines, or in collapsed infrastructure zones can maintain armed capability by harvesting parts from the battlefield. The weapon's performance ceiling is limited by available components, but its performance floor is 'functional firearm from scrap metal.'
cultural_context: The Mongrel is the weapon of improvisation and survival. Every Mongrel is unique — a physical record of what was available, what was scavenged, and what was needed. In Tier 1 communities, Mongrel-building is a respected skill, and gunsmiths who can assemble reliable weapons from random parts are valued members of any settlement. The weapon is ugly, inconsistent, and deeply personal. No two are alike.
story_hooks: A Mongrel recovered from a crime scene contains components from weapons that were supposed to be destroyed in an Arcturus decommissioning. Someone is diverting 'destroyed' weapon parts into the salvage market.

A legendary gunsmith builds Mongrels that outperform factory weapons — their builds are collector's items worth Φ5,000+. They've been kidnapped by a faction that wants exclusive access to their skills.

physical_description.visual_profile: A skeletal, purposefully unfinished SMG with a modular construction that reads as deliberately incomplete — like an assembly kit caught mid-build. The receiver is a flat, geometric polymer-steel hybrid stripped down to functional essentials, with prominent standardized interface points that break the weapon's silhouette into discrete, swappable sections. It looks less like a finished weapon and more like the frame upon which weapons are built.
physical_description.dimensions: Base receiver: 28cm length, 5cm width, 4cm height. Total weapon length with stock: 45-65cm variable. Barrel length: 10-18cm depending on configuration. Overall dimensions shift with component selection.
physical_description.weight_description: Remarkably light in base form (1.5kg empty), but feels deliberately incomplete—like holding a skeleton rather than a finished tool. Weight becomes substantial and unpredictable once components are attached, ranging from balanced to front-heavy depending on barrel and stock selection.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum receiver with integrated polymer interface blocks. Universal attachment points are precision-machined steel bosses. Aesthetic is intentionally industrial and unadorned—function before finish.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with visible machining marks and micro-scratches from repeated component swaps. The aluminum shows wear patterns radiating from each attachment point. Some units bear factory dull-black coating on steel interface bosses, contrasting sharply against the gray aluminum.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray base with charcoal black interface points and attachment bosses. When components are mounted, the mismatched aesthetics of salvaged parts create a deliberately chaotic visual cacophony.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare knurled aluminum or rubberized polymer depending on configuration. The base platform offers no grip—users must attach compatible grips from other weapon systems. This enforces modularity at the most visceral level.
distinctive_features: Twelve visible universal interface points arranged in standardized grid pattern across receiver
Serialized quick-disconnect bosses with color-coded indexing rings to prevent incompatible mating
Exposed bolt carrier visible through top charging slot—no dust cover
Minimalist two-rail system for optics/accessories integration
Kang-Petrov compatibility chart etched into left receiver face
Modular magazine interface with spring-loaded capture tabs
Deliberately asymmetrical receiver—built to accept left or right mounting depending on component selection
Welded reinforcement ribs at stress points, visible as subtle ridges
Empty spaces where components aren't yet installed—functional voids
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: KANG-PETROV ARMS logo stamped above left interface group. Serial number engraved on a replaceable steel plate secured by two universal screws. Tiny 'KPS-3M' marking on receiver. Compatibility codes printed on interface bosses themselves. Multiple warning labels in simplified pictograph format.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field guns appear worn and mismatched—a visual frankenstein of salvaged components in varying conditions. Scratches concentrate around interface points from repeated component swaps. The receiver itself remains pristine due to minimal user contact; the real wear manifests as component incompatibility—slightly bent interface points, stripped quick-disconnect threads, grime accumulation in mating surfaces. Well-used Mongrels look like they were assembled this morning from yesterday's battlefield.

image_prompt: Product photography of a modular SMG receiver laid flat on dark brushed steel surface, angled 45 degrees to showcase the standardized interface points and grid of attachment bosses. Gunmetal gray aluminum receiver with charcoal black precision-machined steel bosses. Dramatic single side-light (neo-noir blue-white) illuminates the interface geometry and etched compatibility markings, casting sharp shadows into the empty modular spaces. One gloved hand (wearing tactical gray polymer gloves) grips the bare aluminum receiver from the side, emphasizing its incompleteness and skeletal design. Shallow depth-of-field. Hyper-detailed close-up showing machining marks, color-coded indexing rings on interface points, and Kang-Petrov branding. Gritty, industrial, deliberately unfinished aesthetic.
